explanation.concept: TCO comparison: cloud removes capex, not opex
explanation.correct: AWS lets a company avoid large upfront capital expenditures (buying racks, data centers, hardware) and replace them with variable, pay-as-you-go operational spend. That shift away from unpredictable capex is the core driver of the AWS TCO Calculator's savings estimates.

distractors.B: AWS runs on a shared responsibility model, but a company remains responsible for its own third-party software license costs and compliance regardless of hosting location.
distractors.C: Moving to AWS trades capex for variable opex; it does not eliminate operational expenditure altogether — you still pay for the resources you consume.
distractors.D: Managed application hosting isn't what drives TCO down here; many AWS workloads (e.g. EC2) still require the customer to manage the application itself.

explanation.concept: Instructor-led learning vs self-serve AWS resources
explanation.correct: AWS Classroom Training and Online Tech Talks are both delivered live by AWS instructors and experts, making them the instructor-led options among the choices. Classroom Training is in-person or virtual instructor-led courses; Online Tech Talks are live webinars run by AWS specialists.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor is an account-inspection tool for cost, performance, and security checks, not a training resource.
distractors.C: The AWS Blog is self-serve written content with no instructor or live session.
distractors.D: AWS Forums are a self-serve, community Q&A resource, not an instructor-led format.

explanation.concept: Console access hardening: authentication factors and policy
explanation.correct: Multi-Factor Authentication adds a second proof of identity beyond the password, and a strong password policy (length, complexity, rotation) raises the bar for guessing or brute-forcing a login. Both directly harden the console sign-in step.

distractors.A: Secrets Manager stores and rotates application secrets like database credentials — it doesn't protect console sign-in.
distractors.B: Certificate Manager issues and manages SSL/TLS certificates for encrypting traffic to services, unrelated to console login security.
distractors.D: Security groups are stateful firewalls for EC2 instances and other resources; they don't govern who can log into the Management Console.

explanation.concept: The VPC dashboard configures networking primitives inside a VPC, not services outside it
explanation.correct: Security Groups and Subnets are both configured from the VPC Dashboard, alongside route tables, NACLs, internet/NAT gateways, and VPC peering — the building blocks of a VPC's own network.

distractors.A: CloudFront is a global content delivery service managed from its own console, not the VPC Dashboard.
distractors.B: Route 53 is AWS's DNS service, managed separately from a VPC's internal networking.
distractors.E: Elastic Load Balancing has its own console; while a load balancer attaches to VPC subnets, it isn't configured from the VPC Dashboard itself.

explanation.concept: Physical security of data centers sits entirely on AWS's side of the shared responsibility line
explanation.correct: AWS designs, builds, and audits the physical security of its data centers (badges, cameras, guards, environmental controls) with no customer visibility or role — auditing that is AWS's sole responsibility.

distractors.A: IAM policies are configured and owned by the customer, who is responsible for auditing their own permission settings.
distractors.C: S3 bucket policies are customer-defined access controls, so auditing them is a customer responsibility.
distractors.D: CloudTrail logs record customer account activity; auditing that log is a customer task, not AWS's.

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing gives one invoice and pooled volume, not free extra limits
explanation.correct: Consolidated billing combines multiple accounts under a single management-account invoice (A), and because usage across all linked accounts is aggregated, the group can cross into higher-volume, lower-price tiers sooner (D).

distractors.B: Service limits are set per account and don't increase automatically just because accounts are consolidated.
distractors.C: There's no fixed discount — savings come from volume pricing and Reserved Instance/Savings Plan sharing, which vary with actual usage.
distractors.E: Each linked account can have its own support plan; the management account's support plan isn't automatically extended to every account.

explanation.concept: Undifferentiated heavy lifting AWS takes off a customer's plate
explanation.correct: AWS-managed database services like RDS handle patching the database engine software and taking automated backups on the customer's behalf, freeing internal IT staff from that recurring maintenance work.

distractors.B: Testing application releases is the customer's own application-layer responsibility; AWS doesn't test a customer's code.
distractors.D: Designing a database schema is a data-modeling decision only the customer's team can make for their own application.
distractors.E: Penetration testing of a customer's own workloads remains the customer's responsibility (subject to AWS's testing policy), not something AWS performs for them.

explanation.concept: Expanding to a new Region is operational, not contractual
explanation.correct: AWS Regions are available to any account already using AWS — there's no separate contract or sign-up. A company expands simply by starting to deploy resources in the new Region.

distractors.A: No new contract is needed; AWS pricing and terms already cover all public Regions under the existing account.
distractors.B: Availability Zones are physically fixed data centers within a Region — they can't be relocated to another Region.
distractors.D: The AWS Management Console is a single global web application; there's no separate per-Region download.

explanation.concept: Elastic Load Balancing's value is adapting to changing traffic
explanation.correct: Elastic Load Balancers distribute incoming traffic across targets and scale their own capacity as traffic patterns shift, which is exactly why they suit workloads with unpredictable or bursty demand.

distractors.A: There's no feature that converts an Application Load Balancer into a Classic Load Balancer — load balancer type is chosen at creation, and each type is managed independently.
distractors.B: This continues the same false claim about converting between load balancer types; the two are separate products with separate configurations.
distractors.D: ELB does automatically adjust capacity, but it is a paid service billed hourly plus usage — it is not provided free of charge.

explanation.concept: One-hour response time starts at the Business plan
explanation.correct: The Business Support plan is the lowest tier offering a guaranteed under-1-hour response time for business-critical, production-system-down cases. Developer and Basic have slower or best-effort response times.

distractors.A: Enterprise also offers fast response times but at a higher cost — it isn't the minimum plan needed.
distractors.C: The Developer plan's fastest response time is well over an hour for system-impaired cases, not under one hour.
distractors.D: The Basic plan includes no case-based technical support with guaranteed response times at all.

explanation.concept: Low-cost plus immediate retrieval rules out archival storage
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 offers durable, low-cost object storage with millisecond retrieval, making it the right fit when backups must stay both cheap and instantly accessible. Glacier is cheaper still but trades away immediate retrieval.

distractors.B: Glacier is cheaper per GB than S3 but retrieval takes minutes to hours, failing the 'immediate retrieval' requirement.
distractors.C: EBS is block storage attached to a single EC2 instance, priced higher than S3 and not designed as a durable backup repository.
distractors.D: EC2 instance store is ephemeral — its contents are lost when the instance stops or terminates, so it's unsuitable for durable backups.

explanation.concept: Professional Services vs Solutions Architects vs Account Managers
explanation.correct: AWS Professional Services is the paid consulting team that helps customers plan and execute cloud adoption across defined specialty practice areas such as migration, security, and DevOps.

distractors.A: Enterprise Support is a support plan tier, not a consulting engagement team.
distractors.B: Solutions Architects provide pre-sales technical guidance; the paid, practice-area-based engagement team is Professional Services.
distractors.D: Account Managers own the commercial relationship, not hands-on paid delivery engagements.

explanation.concept: 24/7 multi-channel support with under-1-hour response starts at Business
explanation.correct: Business Support provides 24/7 phone, email, and chat access with under-1-hour response for production-system-down issues, at a lower cost than Enterprise, which offers the same responsiveness plus extras like a Concierge team.

distractors.A: Basic includes no case-based technical support channels at all.
distractors.B: Developer support is limited to business-hours email access with no guaranteed 1-hour response.
distractors.D: Enterprise meets the requirement but costs more than Business, which already satisfies it — so it isn't the lowest-cost option.

explanation.concept: AWS Config tracks configuration change history; other tools track cost, performance, or vulnerabilities
explanation.correct: AWS Config continuously records configuration changes to AWS resources and evaluates them against rules, making it the service for auditing change management over time.

distractors.B: Trusted Advisor gives point-in-time best-practice checks on cost, security, performance, and limits — it doesn't track a history of configuration changes.
distractors.C: CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs, and alarms for operational performance, not resource configuration history.
distractors.D: Amazon Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities and network exposure on running workloads, not configuration change tracking.

explanation.concept: Trusted Advisor recommends and flags; it doesn't scan software or auto-remediate
explanation.correct: Trusted Advisor inspects the account and surfaces cost-optimization recommendations (B) and flags resources whose permission settings look risky (C) — but it only advises, it doesn't fix anything or scan application code.

distractors.A: Scanning application software for vulnerabilities is Amazon Inspector's job, not Trusted Advisor's.
distractors.D: Trusted Advisor only reports findings; it never automatically changes account settings on the customer's behalf.
distractors.E: Detecting a compromised EC2 instance based on behavior is Amazon GuardDuty's role, not Trusted Advisor's.

explanation.concept: RDS is the managed relational database service
explanation.correct: Amazon RDS provisions, patches, and backs up relational database engines such as MySQL and PostgreSQL as a managed service, which is what 'managed service to host databases' describes.

distractors.A: AWS Batch runs batch computing jobs at scale — it has nothing to do with hosting databases.
distractors.B: AWS Artifact is a portal for compliance reports and agreements, not a compute or database service.
distractors.C: AWS Data Pipeline moves and transforms data between sources on a schedule; it doesn't host a database itself.

explanation.concept: Long-term access key ID / secret access key pairs belong to IAM users
explanation.correct: An IAM user is the identity that can be issued a long-term access key ID and secret access key for programmatic access, such as configuring the AWS CLI.

distractors.A: An IAM group is a collection of users for shared permission assignment; it doesn't itself hold credentials.
distractors.C: An IAM role is assumed temporarily and uses short-lived STS credentials, not a persistent access key pair.
distractors.D: An IAM policy is a JSON permissions document; it has no credentials of its own.

explanation.concept: Data-layer protections are the customer's job under shared responsibility
explanation.correct: Encrypting data at rest is a customer responsibility — AWS provides the encryption tools (e.g. KMS, S3 default encryption), but the customer must choose to enable and configure them for their own data.

distractors.A: Wiping decommissioned disk drives is part of AWS's physical infrastructure decommissioning process.
distractors.B: Firmware updates on physical hardware are managed entirely by AWS as part of infrastructure maintenance.
distractors.D: Network cabling specifications are a physical data-center detail that AWS controls, not the customer.

explanation.concept: EFS is the managed, scalable NFS file system for Linux workloads
explanation.correct: Amazon EFS provides a fully managed, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by many Linux-based EC2 instances and on-premises servers — matching the 'shared file storage' requirement exactly.

distractors.A: S3 is object storage accessed over HTTP APIs, not a mountable file system for servers.
distractors.B: Glacier is cold archival object storage meant for infrequently accessed backups, not shared file access.
distractors.C: EBS volumes attach to a single EC2 instance at a time (with rare multi-attach exceptions) — they aren't a general shared file system.

explanation.concept: Programmatic access needs the access key ID / secret access key pair
explanation.correct: Programmatic access to AWS (CLI, SDKs, API) is authenticated with an access key ID paired with a secret access key — together they function like a username and password for API calls.

distractors.B: AWS has no credential called a 'primary key' for account access.
distractors.D: A user ID alone isn't a valid AWS credential for signing API requests.
distractors.E: There is no AWS credential called a 'secondary key.'

explanation.concept: Shared responsibility includes an intangible shared control: awareness and training
explanation.correct: AWS lists 'Awareness and Training' as a shared control — AWS trains its own employees on security, while customers must train their own staff on how to use AWS securely. Both parties own a piece of it.

distractors.A: Client-side encryption keys for S3 are entirely customer-managed and customer-supplied — AWS has no role in it.
distractors.B: Configuring an EC2 instance (OS, applications, network settings) is entirely a customer responsibility.
distractors.C: Environmental controls of physical data centers are entirely AWS's responsibility, with no customer role.

explanation.concept: Instance store is ephemeral, physically tied to the host
explanation.correct: Amazon EC2 instance store is physically attached, temporary block storage; its data is lost whenever the instance is stopped or terminated, unlike EBS, which persists independently.

distractors.A: EBS volumes persist independently of the instance lifecycle and survive a stop, unless explicitly deleted.
distractors.C: EFS is a durable, persistent network file system, not ephemeral storage tied to one instance.
distractors.D: S3 is durable, persistent object storage that exists independently of any EC2 instance.

explanation.concept: Consolidated billing pools usage to unlock volume pricing tiers
explanation.correct: By combining usage across linked accounts into one bill, consolidated billing lets the whole organization qualify for volume-based pricing discounts sooner than any single account would alone.

distractors.B: Consolidated billing is about billing, not IAM — it doesn't share access permissions between accounts.
distractors.C: Consolidated billing produces a single combined bill, not multiple separate bills.
distractors.D: Tagging for cost allocation is still needed to break down costs by project or team; consolidated billing doesn't remove that need.

explanation.concept: Serverless means no server to provision or patch, whatever the workload type
explanation.correct: AWS Step Functions (serverless workflow orchestration), DynamoDB (serverless NoSQL database), and SNS (serverless pub/sub messaging) all require no server provisioning or capacity management from the customer.

distractors.A: EC2 requires provisioning and managing servers, so this group mixes a non-serverless compute service in with serverless ones.
distractors.B: Kinesis and SQS are serverless, but EMR runs managed clusters of servers that the customer provisions and sizes.
distractors.D: Athena and Cognito are serverless, but EC2 requires the customer to provision and manage the underlying instances.

explanation.concept: Dedicated Hosts expose physical sockets/cores, which is what hardware-bound licenses require
explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts give visibility into the underlying physical server's sockets and cores, letting customers bring existing server-bound software licenses — often tied to physical hardware — into AWS.

distractors.A: Spot Instances are spare capacity sold at a discount with no special licensing accommodation.
distractors.B: Reserved Instances are a billing commitment for capacity discounts, unrelated to physical hardware visibility for licensing.
distractors.D: On-Demand Instances run on shared hardware with no visibility into the physical sockets/cores needed for hardware-bound licenses.

explanation.concept: Least privilege and MFA are the two core account-access hardening practices
explanation.correct: Granting least privilege limits what each IAM user can do if compromised, and MFA adds a second factor beyond the password for privileged users — both directly reduce the risk of account compromise.

distractors.A: CloudTrail records activity for later investigation; it doesn't itself prevent unauthorized access.
distractors.C: Sharing one IAM user among many people is a security anti-pattern — it removes accountability and increases blast radius.
distractors.D: CloudFront is a content delivery service, unrelated to account access security.

explanation.concept: CloudFormation is AWS's infrastructure-as-code service
explanation.correct: AWS CloudFormation lets you define infrastructure in template files (JSON/YAML) and provisions or updates it declaratively, which is exactly what infrastructure as code means.

distractors.A: CodePipeline automates release pipelines (build, test, deploy) — it orchestrates deployments, it doesn't define infrastructure as code.
distractors.B: CodeDeploy automates application code deployment to compute resources; it doesn't provision the infrastructure itself.
distractors.C: Direct Connect is a dedicated network link between on-premises and AWS, unrelated to infrastructure provisioning.

explanation.concept: Multi-AZ protects against a single Availability Zone's failure
explanation.correct: Spreading an application across multiple Availability Zones means a disruption in one AZ (power, network, hardware) doesn't take the whole application down, directly raising availability.

distractors.A: A Region-wide natural disaster can affect multiple AZs simultaneously since they're in the same metro area; multi-Region protects against that, not multi-AZ.
distractors.C: AZs within a Region sit close together for low-latency replication, not spread widely enough to serve a wider geography the way edge locations do.
distractors.D: Multi-AZ deployments can add slight latency from synchronous replication between zones; it isn't primarily a latency-reduction technique.

explanation.concept: Aurora is MySQL-compatible with cloud-native scaling
explanation.correct: Amazon Aurora is compatible with MySQL, offering automatic storage scaling and read replica scaling well beyond what a self-managed MySQL instance provides, while staying wire-compatible with existing MySQL tooling.

distractors.B: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics (OLAP), not a MySQL-compatible transactional database.
distractors.C: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document database, not MySQL-compatible.
distractors.D: ElastiCache is an in-memory cache (Redis/Memcached), not a MySQL-compatible database.

explanation.concept: AWS design principles favor decoupling over tight, monolithic coupling
explanation.correct: Loose coupling — designing components to interact through well-defined interfaces such as queues or APIs rather than direct dependencies — is a core AWS Well-Architected design principle that improves scalability and fault isolation.

distractors.A: AWS design principles push to eliminate single points of failure, not implement them.
distractors.C: AWS favors breaking monoliths into smaller, independently scalable components, not building monolithic designs.
distractors.D: AWS design favors horizontal (elastic) scaling over vertical scaling, which has hard upper limits.

explanation.concept: Concierge and Technical Account Manager are Enterprise-only perks
explanation.correct: The Concierge team — billing and account experts dedicated to Enterprise Support customers — is exclusive to the Enterprise plan and not offered at any lower tier.

distractors.A: Trusted Advisor's core checks are available on every plan; the full check set is available from Business and up, not exclusively Enterprise.
distractors.B: Support cases can be opened at multiple plan tiers (Developer and above), not just Enterprise.
distractors.D: Amazon Connect is a customer-contact-center service, unrelated to AWS Support plan tiers.

explanation.concept: Cloud economics: capex to opex, not the reverse
explanation.correct: On-premises data centers require large upfront capital expenditure for hardware; moving to AWS replaces that with variable, pay-as-you-go operational expenditure — capex becomes opex.

distractors.A: This reverses the actual direction of the shift — cloud moves spend from upfront capex to variable opex, not the other way around.
distractors.B: This mislabels the destination as 'capex' when the AWS pay-as-you-go model is operational expense (opex), not capital expense.
distractors.D: The move doesn't eliminate spending altogether; the company still pays for the resources it consumes, just structured differently.

explanation.concept: Physical isolation for TCO purposes means Dedicated Hosts
explanation.correct: Dedicated Hosts provide a physical server reserved entirely for one customer, which is the compute model that delivers actual physical isolation — the cost of that isolation is what belongs in the TCO analysis.

distractors.B: Reserved Instances are a billing discount on shared, multi-tenant hardware — they don't provide physical isolation.
distractors.C: On-Demand Instances also run on shared multi-tenant hardware with no physical isolation guarantee.
distractors.D: No Upfront Reserved Instances are just a payment-option variant of Reserved Instances, still on shared hardware.

explanation.concept: Glacier is purpose-built for long-term, infrequently accessed archives
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 Glacier is designed specifically for long-term, low-cost archival storage such as data backups that are rarely accessed, trading retrieval speed for a much lower storage price.

distractors.A: RDS is a managed relational database service, not an archival storage tier.
distractors.C: Snowball is a physical device for bulk one-time data transfer into or out of AWS, not an ongoing storage location.
distractors.D: EBS is block storage for active EC2 workloads, priced much higher than Glacier and not intended for long-term archives.

explanation.concept: Phone support begins at the Business plan
explanation.correct: Business Support is the lowest tier that includes phone access to AWS Support alongside email and chat; Developer and Basic have no phone support channel.

distractors.A: Enterprise also includes phone support but costs more than the minimum plan that already offers it.
distractors.C: Developer support is limited to email/web-based contact during business hours — no phone channel.
distractors.D: Basic Support includes no case-based technical support, phone or otherwise.

explanation.concept: Spot trades interruption risk for the deepest discount
explanation.correct: Spot Instances use AWS's spare compute capacity and can be discounted up to 90% off the On-Demand price, in exchange for the instance being reclaimed with short notice when capacity is needed elsewhere.

distractors.A: Reserved Instances offer discounts up to roughly 70-75% for a 1- or 3-year commitment, not 90%.
distractors.B: On-Demand is the standard, undiscounted pay-as-you-go rate — the baseline other pricing models discount from.
distractors.C: Dedicated Hosts can offer license-related savings but don't reach anywhere near a 90% discount off On-Demand.

explanation.concept: S3 stores the video; CloudFront caches it at edge locations for low latency
explanation.correct: Amazon S3 durably stores the video files, and Amazon CloudFront caches and serves that content from edge locations close to viewers, which is what minimizes latency for large-scale video delivery.

distractors.A: 'appGateway' isn't an AWS service name relevant to video content delivery.
distractors.C: EFS is a shared network file system for compute workloads, not a content-delivery mechanism for end users.
distractors.D: Glacier is archival cold storage with retrieval delays of minutes to hours — the opposite of low-latency delivery.

explanation.concept: Edge locations cache and deliver content close to users — they don't run applications
explanation.correct: Edge locations are CloudFront's globally distributed caching points: they deliver content closer to end users (B) and reduce load on the origin server by serving cached responses locally (D).

distractors.A: Edge locations cache and serve content; they don't host full applications the way EC2 or Lambda do.
distractors.C: NoSQL database caching is what DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) or ElastiCache do — not the role of CloudFront edge locations.
distractors.E: Sending notifications to end users is Amazon SNS's job, not an edge location's.

explanation.concept: The TCO Calculator quantifies migration savings before you move
explanation.correct: The AWS TCO Calculator compares the cost of running workloads on-premises versus on AWS and produces a detailed report estimating the savings from migrating — exactly the tool for that use case.

distractors.B: Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts AWS spend after you're already using AWS; it doesn't compare against on-premises costs.
distractors.C: Budgets sets spending thresholds and alerts on AWS usage; it doesn't produce a savings comparison report.
distractors.D: Migration Hub tracks the progress and status of migration tasks across tools, not cost-savings estimates.

explanation.concept: Personal Health Dashboard is customized to your resources; Service Health Dashboard is generic
explanation.correct: AWS Personal Health Dashboard filters AWS service health events down to the ones actually affecting the customer's own resources, giving a personalized operational view rather than a general status page.

distractors.A: The Service Health Dashboard shows the general operational status of AWS services for everyone, not tailored to one account's resources.
distractors.B: X-Ray traces requests through a customer's own application for performance debugging; it doesn't report AWS service health.
distractors.D: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs for a customer's resources, but it doesn't report on the health of the underlying AWS services themselves.

explanation.concept: Offloading infrastructure lets a business focus on its core work
explanation.correct: By having AWS manage the undifferentiated heavy lifting of infrastructure, a business frees its staff and budget to focus on activities that differentiate it competitively, rather than running data centers.

distractors.A: Moving to AWS doesn't eliminate IT bills — usage-based charges replace capital IT costs.
distractors.B: Servers in each customer's own data center describes an on-premises or hybrid model, not a benefit of moving to AWS.
distractors.D: Leaving servers unpatched is a security risk, not a stated benefit of any cloud migration.

explanation.concept: Basic Support has no case-based channel — only self-serve community resources
explanation.correct: The Basic Support plan includes no technical support cases; the way a Basic-plan user gets help is through AWS's self-serve resources like the Discussion Forums, documentation, and Trusted Advisor's core checks.

distractors.A: Senior Support Engineers are engaged through paid case-based support (Business/Enterprise), not included in Basic.
distractors.B: Technical Account Managers are an Enterprise-plan benefit, not available on Basic.
distractors.C: Trusted Advisor's full check set requires Business or Enterprise support; Basic only gets a handful of core checks, not full technical assistance.

explanation.concept: Regional disasters require a multi-Region strategy, not just multi-AZ
explanation.correct: A natural disaster can affect an entire geographic area, including all Availability Zones in a Region, so deploying applications across multiple AWS Regions is what protects against that scale of disruption.

distractors.A: Multiple AZs within one Region protect against a data-center-level failure, but a region-wide disaster can affect all AZs in that Region at once.
distractors.B: Hybrid cloud still keeps infrastructure within the same geographic area unless it explicitly spans other regions, so it doesn't solve a regional disaster.
distractors.D: AWS Artifact is a compliance-document repository, not a mechanism for replicating running applications across Regions.

explanation.concept: Backing up your own data/volumes is a customer responsibility
explanation.correct: Amazon EBS volumes are customer-managed storage; ensuring they're backed up (e.g. via snapshots) is the customer's job under the shared responsibility model, since AWS doesn't decide what data needs preserving.

distractors.A: AWS manages the network connectivity of its own infrastructure to the internet as part of security 'of' the cloud.
distractors.B: Patching the underlying AWS Cloud infrastructure is AWS's responsibility, not the customer's.
distractors.C: Physical security of AWS data centers is entirely AWS's responsibility.

explanation.concept: Spot suits interruption-tolerant, non-critical workloads
explanation.correct: Infrequent, interruptible batch jobs can tolerate being reclaimed with short notice, making them ideal for Spot Instances, which trade that interruption risk for up to 90% savings over On-Demand.

distractors.A: A main production website needs consistent availability, which doesn't tolerate Spot's interruption risk.
distractors.B: A 99.999% uptime SLA requires highly reliable capacity, which Spot Instances — reclaimable at any time — can't guarantee.
distractors.C: A heavily used legacy database needs steady, uninterrupted compute, unsuited to Spot's reclaim behavior.

explanation.concept: Region selection weighs latency to users and legal/data-residency requirements
explanation.correct: Choosing a Region closer to end users reduces network latency (A), and some workloads must keep data within specific jurisdictions for legal or regulatory reasons — data sovereignty (C). Both are standard Region-selection criteria alongside cost, services offered, and compliance.

distractors.B: AWS doesn't localize an application's UI language based on Region choice — that's an application-level concern, not infrastructure.
distractors.D: AWS data centers use sophisticated cooling systems regardless of climate; the customer doesn't pay a separate 'cooling cost' that varies by Region choice.
distractors.E: Physical proximity to a company's own office isn't a technical factor AWS documents as a Region-selection criterion — Regions are chosen for infrastructure and compliance needs, not office visits.

explanation.concept: Personal Health Dashboard alerts on events affecting your specific resources
explanation.correct: AWS Personal Health Dashboard proactively alerts a customer when an AWS operational event is likely to affect that customer's specific resources, unlike the general Service Health Dashboard.

distractors.B: The Service Health Dashboard reports overall AWS service status for all customers, without targeting alerts to any one account's resources.
distractors.C: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice recommendations on cost, security, and performance — it doesn't alert on AWS operational events.
distractors.D: Infrastructure Event Management is a paid Enterprise engagement for planning specific events (e.g. product launches), not an automated alerting service.

explanation.concept: The DR spectrum: cost and complexity rise as downtime risk falls
explanation.correct: Multi-site active-active runs full production capacity in more than one location simultaneously, so if one site fails, the other is already serving live traffic — giving it the lowest probability of downtime among the four DR strategies.

distractors.A: Backup and restore is the slowest and cheapest strategy, with the highest downtime risk since infrastructure must be rebuilt from backups.
distractors.B: Pilot light keeps only core systems running at minimal capacity, requiring scale-up time before full recovery — more downtime risk than active-active.
distractors.C: Warm standby runs a scaled-down but functional copy that needs to scale up during failover, which still introduces some downtime versus an already-active second site.

explanation.concept: CodeCommit is AWS's managed Git repository service
explanation.correct: AWS CodeCommit is a fully managed source control service hosting private Git repositories, making version control its primary purpose.

distractors.A: CodeStar provides a unified project dashboard across the whole CI/CD toolchain; it doesn't itself store code history.
distractors.B: The AWS CLI is a tool for interacting with AWS services from a terminal — it isn't a version control system.
distractors.C: Cognito manages user sign-up, sign-in, and access control for applications, unrelated to source control.

explanation.concept: MFA plus a strong password policy are the two direct sign-in hardening controls
explanation.correct: Enabling MFA adds a second authentication factor beyond the password, and enforcing a strong password policy (length, complexity, expiration) raises the difficulty of guessing or cracking credentials — both directly strengthen account logon security.

distractors.A: Certificate Manager issues TLS/SSL certificates for encrypting traffic to services — unrelated to console logon.
distractors.C: Cognito manages authentication for a customer's own application's end users, not AWS account console logons.
distractors.E: AWS Organizations manages multi-account structure and consolidated billing/policies; it doesn't itself add a logon security control.
